files_summary.commands.json:
Array of objects, each representing a command available in the Terminal environment. Each object contains:
- "name": the command name (e.g., "ls", "git").
- "description": a concise description sourced from TLDR pages or command help output.
- "category": logical grouping such as "File Management", "Networking", "System Information", "Compression/Archiving", "Version Control", "Programming", "Container Management", "Process Management", "Security", or "Miscellaneous".
The file includes entries for all commands listed in the environment definition (e.g., dirname, python, traceroute, file, netstat, cut, clear, find, cp, git, ping, curl, basename, tail, sort, history, md5sum, gunzip, which, mv, sha256sum, touch, pwd, gzip, wget, zip, ps, cat, diff, stat, more, env, head, ifconfig, uniq, du, tar, mkdir, nslookup, kubectl, realpath, date, hostname, df, wc, tr, echo, awk, rm, chmod, sed, ls, unzip, whoami, less, grep, cd, helm, tree).
files_summary.toolsets.json:
JSON object describing the Terminal toolset:
- "toolset_name": "Terminal".
- "description": Brief description of the environment providing command execution and security introspection.
- "tools": Array of tool definitions:
  * "run_command": Executes a single CLI command in the `/workspace/dumps/workspace` directory, supporting all standard shell operators. Parameters: `command` (string, required).
  * "show_security_rules": Returns the allowed commands and operations in this environment. No parameters.
- "allowed_shell_operators": true (indicates that shell operators like &&, ||, |, >, etc., are permitted).
- "default_directory": "/workspace/dumps/workspace".
files_summary.security_rules.json:
JSON object defining security configuration for the Terminal service:
- "allow_shell_operators": true.
- "allowed_commands": List of all command names extracted from `commands.json` (e.g., "dirname", "python", "traceroute", … "tree").
- "disallowed_commands": Empty array (no commands are explicitly blocked).
- "allowed_tools": ["run_command", "show_security_rules"].
files_summary.README.md: Schema, lifecycles and business rules of this benchmark's datastore.
files_summary.users.json:
JSON array of 10 user objects. Each object contains:
- user_id (e.g., "U0001")
- username (e.g., "user1")
- email (e.g., "user1@example.com")
- entity (always "example-team")
- created_at (ISO‑8601 timestamp).
files_summary.projects.json:
JSON array of 5 project objects for the entity "example-team". Each object includes:
- name (project slug, e.g., "image-classification")
- entity
- description
- visibility ("public" or "private")
- created_at / updated_at (ISO timestamps)
- tags (list of 3 descriptive tags).
files_summary.runs.csv:
CSV file with 100 synthetic run records (plus header). Columns:
- run_id (8‑character alphanumeric ID)
- project_name (one of the 5 projects)
- display_name (human‑readable name, e.g., "image-classification_run_3")
- state ("finished", "running" or "failed")
- created_at (ISO timestamp)
- accuracy (float, 0.6‑0.99)
- loss (float, 0.1‑2.0)
- learning_rate (float, e.g., 0.0001)
- batch_size (16/32/64/128)
- epochs (5/10/20/50)
- user_id (links to a user in users.json).
files_summary.artifacts.json:
JSON array of 50 artifact entries (10 per project). Each artifact includes:
- artifact_id (unique ID)
- project_name
- name (e.g., "image-classification_artifact_7")
- version (e.g., "v3")
- digest (UUID hex string)
- size_bytes (1 MiB – 1 GiB)
- created_at (ISO timestamp)
- metadata object with fields:
  • framework ("torch", "tensorflow" or "jax")
  • model_type (e.g., "resnet", "bert", "gpt", "dqn", "vae")
  • description (text describing the artifact).
files_summary.traces.json:
JSON array of 227 Weave trace objects (roots + children). Each trace record contains:
- id (unique sequential ID like "T000001")
- trace_id (UUID shared among related traces)
- parent_id (null for root traces; otherwise points to the parent trace id)
- project_name (one of the 5 projects)
- op_name (URI style string, e.g., "weave:///root_op_4")
- display_name (readable label)
- started_at / ended_at (ISO timestamps)
- status ("success" or "error")
- latency_ms (integer)
- costs object with:
  • prompt_tokens_total_cost (float)
  • completion_tokens_total_cost (float)
  • total_cost (sum of the two)
- attributes object with:
  • model_name (e.g., "gpt-4")
  • token_count (integer).
The traces reflect a realistic parent‑child hierarchy (15 root traces per project, each with 1‑3 child traces).

tool_schemas.name: list_commands
tool_schemas.description: Lists the terminal commands available in this environment and returns each command’s name, description, and category, optionally filtered to a single category. Requests are refused when a category filter is provided but is not a string or includes unexpected extra fields. If the category is well-formed but no commands belong to it, nothing is returned for that filter.

category.description: Optional category to filter commands by (e.g., "File Management", "Networking").

tool_schemas.name: get_command
tool_schemas.description: Returns the full definition for a single terminal command identified by its name. Requests are refused when the name is missing, not a string, or empty. The request is also refused when no command with that name exists in this environment.

name.description: The name of the command to retrieve.

tool_schemas.name: list_commands_by_category
tool_schemas.description: Returns all terminal commands that belong to the specified category. Requests are refused when category is missing, not a string, or empty. The request is also refused when the category does not exist or has no commands assigned to it.

category.description: The category to filter commands by (e.g., "File Management", "Networking").

tool_schemas.name: get_toolset
tool_schemas.description: Returns the definition of a named terminal toolset, including its description, included tools, allowed shell operators, and default working directory. Requests are refused when toolset_name is missing, not a string, empty, or when extra fields are provided. The request is also refused when the named toolset is not defined.

toolset_name.description: The name of the toolset to retrieve.

tool_schemas.name: get_security_rules
tool_schemas.description: Returns the current terminal security rules, including which commands and tools are allowed or disallowed and which shell operators are permitted. This endpoint refuses requests that include any parameters or unexpected fields. It may also refuse access when the caller is not permitted to view security policy for this environment.

tool_schemas.name: get_readme
tool_schemas.description: Returns the service’s README documentation content that explains the environment data and intended usage. This endpoint refuses requests that include any parameters or unexpected fields. It may also refuse access when the caller is not permitted to view service documentation.

tool_schemas.name: list_users
tool_schemas.description: Lists users known to the service and returns user objects, optionally filtered by entity, username, and/or email. Requests are refused when any filter is not a string, or when unexpected extra fields are provided. If the filters are valid but no users match, an empty result is returned.

entity.description: Optional entity/organization name to filter users by.

username.description: Optional exact username to filter users by.

email.description: Optional exact email address to filter users by.

tool_schemas.name: get_user
tool_schemas.description: Returns a single user object identified by user_id. Requests are refused when user_id is missing, not a string, or empty. The request is also refused when no user exists with that identifier.

user_id.description: The identifier of the user, e.g., "U0001".

tool_schemas.name: list_projects
tool_schemas.description: Lists projects tracked by the service and returns project objects, optionally filtered by entity, visibility, and/or tag membership. Requests are refused when entity or tag are not strings, when visibility is provided but is not one of the supported values, or when unexpected extra fields are provided. If the filters are valid but no projects match, an empty result is returned.

entity.description: Optional entity/organization name to filter projects by.

visibility.description: Optional visibility filter for returned projects.

tag.description: Optional tag to filter projects by (matches entries in the project's `tags` array).

tool_schemas.name: get_project
tool_schemas.description: Returns a single project object identified by its project_name slug. Requests are refused when project_name is missing, not a string, or empty. The request is also refused when no project exists with that name, or when the project is not visible to the caller.

project_name.description: The slug/name of the project, e.g., "image-classification".

tool_schemas.name: list_runs
tool_schemas.description: Lists recorded runs, returning run records optionally filtered by project, state, launching user, accuracy/loss ranges, batch size, and epochs. It refuses requests where numeric range filters are invalid or contradictory (for example, a minimum greater than its maximum) or where numeric/integer filters are not valid numbers. It may also refuse unsupported state values rather than attempting a partial match.

project_name.description: Filter runs belonging to a specific project.

user_id.description: Filter by the user who launched the run.

min_accuracy.description: Include runs with accuracy greater than or equal to this value.

max_accuracy.description: Include runs with accuracy less than or equal to this value.

min_loss.description: Include runs with loss greater than or equal to this value.

max_loss.description: Include runs with loss less than or equal to this value.

batch_size.description: Filter runs that used a specific batch size.

epochs.description: Filter runs that were trained for a specific number of epochs.

tool_schemas.name: get_run
tool_schemas.description: Retrieves a single run record by run_id and returns the stored run fields for that run. It refuses requests missing run_id, with a run_id that is not an 8-character alphanumeric identifier, or where no run exists with that id. It also refuses access when the run is not visible to the caller under the service’s project/user access rules.

run_id.description: The 8‑character alphanumeric ID of the run.

tool_schemas.name: list_artifacts
tool_schemas.description: Lists artifacts and returns artifact entries optionally filtered by project name, ML framework, and model type. It refuses requests that specify a framework outside the supported set or that provide filter values that fail basic validation (for example, empty identifiers where a value is provided). It also refuses results that the caller is not permitted to view for the referenced project.

project_name.description: Filter artifacts belonging to a specific project.

framework.description: Filter by the ML framework used.

tool_schemas.name: get_artifact
tool_schemas.description: Retrieves a single artifact entry by artifact_id and returns its recorded metadata. It refuses requests missing artifact_id, with an empty or malformed identifier, or where no artifact exists with that id. It also refuses access when the artifact belongs to a project the caller cannot view.

artifact_id.description: The unique identifier of the artifact.

tool_schemas.name: list_traces
tool_schemas.description: Lists execution traces and returns trace records optionally filtered by project, status, parent trace id, and an operation-name substring match. It refuses requests that specify a status outside the supported values or that provide malformed identifiers for parent_id when supplied. It also refuses access to traces for projects the caller is not allowed to view.

project_name.description: Filter traces belonging to a specific project.

parent_id.description: Return only child traces of the given parent trace ID.

op_name_contains.description: Return traces whose `op_name` contains this substring.

tool_schemas.name: get_trace
tool_schemas.description: Retrieves a single trace by trace_id and returns the trace record associated with that UUID. It refuses requests missing trace_id, with a trace_id that is not a valid UUID, or where no trace exists with that id. It also refuses access when the trace is not visible to the caller under the service’s project access rules.

trace_id.description: The UUID identifying the trace (shared among related spans).

metadata.name: Aegis CommandOps Registry
metadata.description: A governed catalog for approved terminal commands and toolsets that also tracks users, ML-style projects, runs, artifacts, and execution traces for auditability and reproducibility.
